title: Why AI can't count letters

beats.say: Ask an AI how many R's are in strawberry, and for years most of them said two.
Here's why. AI never sees letters. It reads tokens: chunks of text, each turned into a number.

vis.note: Example split. Every model chops text differently.

beats.say: So to the model, strawberry is three numbers, not ten letters.
Counting R's means looking inside chunks it never actually sees.
Roughly, a thousand tokens is about seven hundred and fifty words. That's what AI pricing and limits are measured in.

vis.label: ≈ 750 English words
vis.sub: what AI usage is billed in

beats.say: Letters are invisible. Tokens are everything.

caption: Why did AI struggle to count the R's in "strawberry"? It never sees letters. Text is chopped into tokens, chunks that each become a number, so the letters inside a chunk are invisible to it. It's also why AI pricing and context limits are measured in tokens, not words.
sources: OpenAI tokenizer guide: 1 token ≈ 4 characters ≈ 3/4 of a word in English (rule of thumb)
Token split shown is illustrative; exact splits vary by model
